items.description: Portable things lying loose in this place that a player could pick up and carry away. Empty is the right answer for most rooms.

name.description: What the thing is called, as a player would type it to pick it up. A short noun phrase, 1 to 4 words, lower case unless it is a proper name. Never the name of a person or of a place.

description.description: What it is and what state it is in, consistent with the description of the room you just wrote. One or two sentences.

use_kind.description: The engine's physical profile: ordinary unless it is food, a drink, a healing dose, a firestarter, a prying lever, lockpicks, or a key. Choose healing only for an actual restorative dose allowed by this world. Profiles supply behavior from code, never from the description.

combustible.description: True only if this portable thing can be destroyed by an ordinary carried firestarter: dry paper, cloth or wood. False for stone, metal, liquids, or anything uncertain.

readable.description: True only if this thing has WRITING on it that a player could read: a note, a letter, a label, a docket, a page, a sign, an inscription. False for everything else, which is most things.

inscription.description: The words written on it, exactly as they appear, and only when `readable` is true. Write what is actually on the thing -- what a player would read off it -- not a description of it. A few words, a line, or a few short lines; well under the limit, and finished rather than trailing off. Leave this out entirely when nothing is written on it.

people.description: The 2 people who are in this place right now. Write all 2 the instructions describe, in the order they are given there.

fullname.description: Their full name, as a player would type it to speak to them. 2 or 3 words.

nickname.description: What they are called to their face. 1 or 2 words.

appearance.description: What somebody walking in sees of them, consistent with the room you just wrote and with the race and age you were given for them. One or two sentences.

personality.description: How they behave and how they treat a stranger. One or two sentences.

backstory.description: Why they are in this place and what they want. Third person, by name. Two or three sentences.

likes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they enjoy.

dislikes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they cannot stand.

fears.description: A comma separated list of 1 or 2 things they are afraid of.

conscious_desire.description: What this person would say if somebody asked them what they want, today, in this story. Specific, and reachable by somebody standing in a room in this world. Name something to move TOWARD, never something to stop or escape. One sentence, third person, by name.

unconscious_desire.description: What they are actually pursuing and would deny if you said it to them. It sits at an angle to the conscious desire rather than agreeing with it: the conscious desire is the reason they give themselves, and this is what keeps them going when that reason runs out. One sentence, third person, by name.

recognized_need.description: Something they know they must do whether they want to or not, and may resent. A real obligation this world imposes on them -- their work, their family, their debt, their oath, their body -- and one that can get in the way of the conscious desire. One sentence, third person, by name.

unrecognized_need.description: What they need and cannot see, not even unconsciously. A reader should be able to see it from the backstory above while they cannot. If they never do it, pursuing the conscious desire ruins them. It must not be the conscious desire said twice. One sentence, third person, by name.

need_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the UNRECOGNIZED NEED has. It may be the same label as the one above; the more interesting answer is usually a different one.

The air is thick with the scent of polished moonstone and the faint, metallic tang of old machinery, humming just below hearing. Towering spires of white marble and silver filigree rise around you, their surfaces catching the pale glow of the ever-present lanterns, casting long, unmoving shadows. A wide, circular plaza stretches before you, its center dominated by a massive, inlaid compass rose of black obsidian and silver, its needle pointing unerringly north despite the city’s chaos beyond these borders. The silence here is deliberate, broken only by the distant, measured footsteps of guards in silver armor.
detail.lore: The Sovereign’s Circle is the only district in Nocturnis where the residual magic of Nocturna has been suppressed, its rearrangements halted by ancient Lunar Sovereign technology embedded in the bedrock. Built as the seat of power for the Sovereigns, it houses their palaces, archives, and the Celestial Spire, a tower said to pierce the veil between the mortal world and the lunar realm. The plaza’s compass rose is a relic of the pre-war era, its mechanisms still functional, serving as both a symbol of control and a practical tool for navigators. The district is heavily guarded, its borders patrolled to ensure no unauthorized person disrupts the delicate balance that keeps it static.

## Universe Details
physics: This world adheres to standard physical laws, with one exception: the city of Nocturnis, built on the ruins of an ancient war, rearranges itself every night due to the residual magical energy from the Great War. This energy, called Nocturna, is harnessed from the moon and causes buildings, streets, and landmarks to shift and change. The effects of Nocturna are limited to the city boundaries, and its influence wanes during the day, allowing the city to remain static until nightfall. Nocturna does not affect living beings directly, but prolonged exposure can cause disorientation and memory loss. The city's rearrangement follows certain patterns, often influenced by the phases of the moon, but these patterns are complex and not fully understood.
technology: Technology in this world is a blend of pre-war remnants and post-war innovations. The Great War, which ended 75 years ago, left behind advanced but often broken or dangerous technology. The current society has managed to salvage and repurpose some of this tech, but much of it remains beyond their understanding. Most people rely on steam-powered machinery and simple electronics. The city of Nocturnis has a unique technology called Lunar Compasses, which are devices that can predict the city's nightly rearrangements with about 60% accuracy. These compasses are highly sought after but require rare moonstones to function.
geographies: The world is dominated by the ever-changing city of Nocturnis, surrounded by a vast, desolate landscape known as the Scorch. The Scorch is a reminder of the Great War, a wasteland where little life thrives. To the north lies the Crystal Peaks, a mountain range rich in moonstones. To the east, the Verdant Expanse is a vast forest that has begun to reclaim the land. Within Nocturnis, notable landmarks include the Ever-Shifting Bazaar, a marketplace that changes location and layout every night, and the Celestial Spire, a tower that remains static despite the city's rearrangements. The city is divided into districts, each with its unique characteristics, such as the Industrial Quarter, the Residential Loop, and the Sovereign's Circle.
races: Crystal Dwarves, Lunar Sovereigns, Nocturna-Blighted, Scorch Nomads, Verdant Folk
civilizations: The city of Nocturnis is the center of civilization, ruled by the Lunar Sovereigns who control the supply of moonstones and advanced technology. The Sovereigns live in the opulent Sovereign's Circle, while the rest of the population resides in the ever-changing districts. The Scorch Nomads roam the wasteland, trading scavenged pre-war technology and resources with the Verdant Folk and Crystal Dwarves. The Verdant Folk live in harmony with nature in the Verdant Expanse, while the Crystal Dwarves mine moonstones in the Crystal Peaks. Tensions exist between the Lunar Sovereigns and the other factions due to the Sovereigns' control of resources and technology, as well as their secretive and hierarchical nature.


## Story Details
title: The Lunar Cartographer
genre: Fantasy
preface: The apartment smells of boiled cabbage and lamp oil. A fine dust of plaster drifts down from the ceiling where the building groans, settling itself into its new configuration for the night. You sit at the oak table by the window, watching motes swirl in the amber light of your kerosene lamp. Across the scarred wood, a half-finished map of Nocturnis spreads out like a rumor you can't quite believe. The Larkspur Quarter, where you woke this morning, has already migrated two blocks north by your last bearings. The Bell of Saint Aravel chimes once in the distance—11 p.m., or close enough. Outside the open window, the cobblestones of Mournwell Lane breathe with a faint, silvery luminescence, rearranging themselves with the patience of something that has done this for seventy-five years. Your landlord, old Grenn, has left a note under your door demanding the overdue rent by morning, or he'll have your table and your instruments out in the lane by noon. The map is worth more than the rent. Both are due before the city forgets where it put this building.
summary: The player is a cartographer hired by the Lunar Sovereigns to map the nightly rearrangements of the city of Nocturnis, where buildings, streets, and landmarks shift with the moon's phases due to residual magical energy called Nocturna. As they work, they uncover conspiracies within the Sovereigns, encounter the displaced peoples of the Scorch Nomads and Verdant Folk, and grapple with the disorienting effects of prolonged exposure to Nocturna, which causes memory loss. The game's tone is grounded, atmospheric, and focused on mystery and survival in a world that refuses to stay still.


## The Place
name: Sovereign's Circle
teaser: The Sovereigns' own ground, where the streets have been made to hold still.

## Instructions
Write this place out in full.
- The description is what the player reads on arrival. Address them as "you"

  the player noticing

## Who Is Here
Write EXACTLY 2 people who are in this place right now.
- Anyone you write is somebody the player can walk up to and talk to, so they
  have to have a reason to be standing here and something they want
- Do not write the player, and do not write somebody passing through

  spoken for above

Who they are is already decided. Write these people and do not change them:
  the 1st is Verdant Folk, about 60, non-binary
  the 2nd is Verdant Folk, about 31, male

## Their Four Objects of Desire

Write four things this person is after and pick two labels for them. Work from
everything above -- their backstory, what they like and dislike, what they are
afraid of, how old they are, how strong their will is, and where they are
standing.

The two labels are picked from this list and nothing else:

  keep     They are holding on to something they already have.
  obtain   They are trying to get hold of something they do not have.
  reach    They are trying to get to a particular place.
  attend   They are trying to stay near a particular person.
  avoid    They are trying to get away from a person or a place.
  withhold They are trying to stop somebody else getting something.
  offer    They are trying to put something into somebody else's hands.

Rules:
- Every one of the four names something to move TOWARD. A field that only says
  what they want to stop or escape is not finished. Say what is on the other
  side of it.
- Write them so an ordinary act in a room could serve one: picking something
  up, handing something over, walking out, staying put, standing near
  somebody. Do not write a desire nobody could act on in a room.
- Keep them consistent with the fears and dislikes above. A fear is usually the
  shadow of one of these four and should read that way.
- The conscious desire and the unrecognized need must not be the same thing
  said twice.
- Write in the third person, by name.
- Do not resolve any of them, and do not say how the story ends.
- Respect the stated length of each field.
- Each person in this room gets their own four. Two people in one room must not
  want the same thing in the same words.
- At least one of them should want something that is in this room or one step
  out of it.

history.content:
## Universe Details
physics: Gravity is consistent at 9.8 m/s², but the world is veined with ley lines—thin, invisible rivers of latent magic that pulse at a frequency of 0.3 Hz, detectable only by iron-forged compasses. These lines can be tapped by blood rituals, but each use drains the caster’s lifespan by exactly one day per minute of magic. The ley lines are finite; overuse in a region causes them to fade for a century. No magic can resurrect the dead or heal mortal wounds, only delay them.
technology: The world is locked in a late medieval stasis, with iron and steel as the primary metals. Clockwork mechanisms exist but are rare, limited to devices no larger than a loaf of bread due to the scarcity of precision gears. Gunpowder is known but unstable, often exploding prematurely in 1 out of 5 attempts. Most advancements are suppressed by the Church of the Eternal Pyre, which burns any invention deemed heretical.
geographies: The kingdom of Durnhold is a land of jagged iron cliffs and black pine forests, its heart dominated by the Ashen Spire, a dead volcano where the Church burns heretics. The goblin caves lie beneath the Spire’s roots, a labyrinth of obsidian tunnels lit by bioluminescent fungi that dim every 12 hours. The nearest town, Hollow’s End, is a day’s ride north, its walls built from the bones of ancient trolls. The river Veyth, wide and slow, marks the border between Durnhold and the goblin territories, its waters undrinkable due to high iron content.
races: Durnish, Goblins, Trollkin, Veythi
civilizations: The Kingdom of Durnhold is ruled by the Iron Council, a cabal of knights and priests who enforce the Church’s decrees from the Obsidian Throne in the capital, Spire’s Rest. The goblins are divided into warring clans, the largest being the Blackfang, who control the dungeon where the prince is held. The Trollkin have no settlements, only nomadic bands, while the Veythi operate from floating barges on the river, their only permanent structure being the Rust Market, a black-market hub hidden in the river’s mist. The uneasy peace is maintained by the Iron Council’s threat of annihilation and the goblins’ fear of open war, but raids and executions are common.


## Story Details
title: The Iron Gate Descends
genre: dark fantasy
preface: The iron gate groans as it settles into the stone, its teeth biting into the threshold with a finality that echoes through the cavern. You stand in the dim glow of bioluminescent fungi, the air thick with the scent of damp earth and old blood. Your gauntleted hand rests on the hilt of your Veldarian sword, its edge still sharp despite the weight of the blackened plate armor pressing into your shoulders. The prince’s signet ring, cold in your palm, was found in the mud outside this gate—proof he passed this way. Behind you, the tunnel slopes upward, but the way forward is a yawning maw of obsidian, the walls slick with moisture. Somewhere in the dark, something skitters.
summary: A Durnish knight, clad in heavy blackened plate, stands at the threshold of the goblin caves beneath the Ashen Spire, having just forced open an iron gate. The prince’s signet ring, discovered in the mud, confirms his passage into the tunnels. The air is thick with the scent of damp earth and the faint glow of fungi, while the distant sound of movement hints at unseen dangers ahead. The Church’s decree to retrieve the prince or die trying weighs heavily, but the immediate threat is the darkness itself.

description.description: What the player sees, hears and smells standing in this place right now. Describe THIS place only -- not what neighbours it, not what is visible out of a window or across the way, because the world around it can move. Second person. One paragraph, 4 to 6 sentences.

lore.description: What this place is, who made it and what happened here. Written for the game engine rather than the player. One paragraph, 3 to 5 sentences.

name.description: What this room is called -- ONLY when the instructions above ask you to name it. Leave this out entirely otherwise. A short noun phrase a player would type to walk into it, carrying the article English wants on it: "the counting room". Never the name of the building it is in, never a name this story has already given to a room, a person or a thing, and never a comma.

items.description: Portable things lying loose in this place that a player could pick up and carry away. Empty is the right answer for most rooms.

name.description: What the thing is called, as a player would type it to pick it up. A short noun phrase, 1 to 4 words, lower case unless it is a proper name. Never the name of a person or of a place.

description.description: What it is and what state it is in, consistent with the description of the room you just wrote. One or two sentences.

use_kind.description: The engine's physical profile: ordinary unless it is food, a drink, a healing dose, a firestarter, a prying lever, lockpicks, or a key. Choose healing only for an actual restorative dose allowed by this world. Profiles supply behavior from code, never from the description.

combustible.description: True only if this portable thing can be destroyed by an ordinary carried firestarter: dry paper, cloth or wood. False for stone, metal, liquids, or anything uncertain.

readable.description: True only if this thing has WRITING on it that a player could read: a note, a letter, a label, a docket, a page, a sign, an inscription. False for everything else, which is most things.

inscription.description: The words written on it, exactly as they appear, and only when `readable` is true. Write what is actually on the thing -- what a player would read off it -- not a description of it. A few words, a line, or a few short lines; well under the limit, and finished rather than trailing off. Leave this out entirely when nothing is written on it.

people.description: The person who is in this place right now. Write the one the instructions describe.

fullname.description: Their full name, as a player would type it to speak to them. 2 or 3 words.

nickname.description: What they are called to their face. 1 or 2 words.

appearance.description: What somebody walking in sees of them, consistent with the room you just wrote and with the race and age you were given for them. One or two sentences.

personality.description: How they behave and how they treat a stranger. One or two sentences.

backstory.description: Why they are in this place and what they want. Third person, by name. Two or three sentences.

likes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they enjoy.

dislikes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they cannot stand.

fears.description: A comma separated list of 1 or 2 things they are afraid of.

conscious_desire.description: What this person would say if somebody asked them what they want, today, in this story. Specific, and reachable by somebody standing in a room in this world. Name something to move TOWARD, never something to stop or escape. One sentence, third person, by name.

unconscious_desire.description: What they are actually pursuing and would deny if you said it to them. It sits at an angle to the conscious desire rather than agreeing with it: the conscious desire is the reason they give themselves, and this is what keeps them going when that reason runs out. One sentence, third person, by name.

recognized_need.description: Something they know they must do whether they want to or not, and may resent. A real obligation this world imposes on them -- their work, their family, their debt, their oath, their body -- and one that can get in the way of the conscious desire. One sentence, third person, by name.

unrecognized_need.description: What they need and cannot see, not even unconsciously. A reader should be able to see it from the backstory above while they cannot. If they never do it, pursuing the conscious desire ruins them. It must not be the conscious desire said twice. One sentence, third person, by name.

desire_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the CONSCIOUS DESIRE has -- the one that fits the act they would take tomorrow morning.

need_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the UNRECOGNIZED NEED has. It may be the same label as the one above; the more interesting answer is usually a different one.

history.content:
## Universe Details
physics: Gravity is consistent at 9.8 m/s², but the world is veined with ley lines—thin, invisible rivers of latent magic that pulse at a frequency of 0.3 Hz, detectable only by iron-forged compasses. These lines can be tapped by blood rituals, but each use drains the caster’s lifespan by exactly one day per minute of magic. The ley lines are finite; overuse in a region causes them to fade for a century. No magic can resurrect the dead or heal mortal wounds, only delay them.
technology: The world is locked in a late medieval stasis, with iron and steel as the primary metals. Clockwork mechanisms exist but are rare, limited to devices no larger than a loaf of bread due to the scarcity of precision gears. Gunpowder is known but unstable, often exploding prematurely in 1 out of 5 attempts. Most advancements are suppressed by the Church of the Eternal Pyre, which burns any invention deemed heretical.
geographies: The kingdom of Durnhold is a land of jagged iron cliffs and black pine forests, its heart dominated by the Ashen Spire, a dead volcano where the Church burns heretics. The goblin caves lie beneath the Spire’s roots, a labyrinth of obsidian tunnels lit by bioluminescent fungi that dim every 12 hours. The nearest town, Hollow’s End, is a day’s ride north, its walls built from the bones of ancient trolls. The river Veyth, wide and slow, marks the border between Durnhold and the goblin territories, its waters undrinkable due to high iron content.
races: Durnish, Goblins, Trollkin, Veythi
civilizations: The Kingdom of Durnhold is ruled by the Iron Council, a cabal of knights and priests who enforce the Church’s decrees from the Obsidian Throne in the capital, Spire’s Rest. The goblins are divided into warring clans, the largest being the Blackfang, who control the dungeon where the prince is held. The Trollkin have no settlements, only nomadic bands, while the Veythi operate from floating barges on the river, their only permanent structure being the Rust Market, a black-market hub hidden in the river’s mist. The uneasy peace is maintained by the Iron Council’s threat of annihilation and the goblins’ fear of open war, but raids and executions are common.


## Story Details
title: The Iron Gate Descends
genre: dark fantasy
preface: The iron gate groans as it settles into the stone, its teeth biting into the threshold with a finality that echoes through the cavern. You stand in the dim glow of bioluminescent fungi, the air thick with the scent of damp earth and old blood. Your gauntleted hand rests on the hilt of your Veldarian sword, its edge still sharp despite the weight of the blackened plate armor pressing into your shoulders. The prince’s signet ring, cold in your palm, was found in the mud outside this gate—proof he passed this way. Behind you, the tunnel slopes upward, but the way forward is a yawning maw of obsidian, the walls slick with moisture. Somewhere in the dark, something skitters.
summary: A Durnish knight, clad in heavy blackened plate, stands at the threshold of the goblin caves beneath the Ashen Spire, having just forced open an iron gate. The prince’s signet ring, discovered in the mud, confirms his passage into the tunnels. The air is thick with the scent of damp earth and the faint glow of fungi, while the distant sound of movement hints at unseen dangers ahead. The Church’s decree to retrieve the prince or die trying weighs heavily, but the immediate threat is the darkness itself.

  bolted to it -- something a person could put in a pocket or under an arm

  the player noticing

  default. Food and drink can be consumed without healing; healing is only
  a restorative dose this world permits. Firestarters burn combustible
  objects, levers pry jammed passages, lockpicks try locks, and a key only
  opens a passage explicitly matched to it. Mark combustible only when an
  ordinary firestarter can destroy the object. The engine owns the effects
  and their amounts; its description cannot grant extra powers

  docket, a page, a sign -- mark it readable and WRITE OUT WHAT IS WRITTEN
  ON IT, exactly as it appears on the thing. The words themselves, not a
  description of them, and short enough to finish -- a few words, a line,
  or a few short lines. The game keeps those words and a player reading it
  twice reads the same ones

  have to have a reason to be standing here and something they want

  attend   They are trying to stay near a particular person.
  avoid    They are trying to get away from a person or a place.
  withhold They are trying to stop somebody else getting something.
  offer    They are trying to put something into somebody else's hands.

- Respect the stated length of each field.

detail.lore: The obsidian maw is a natural fissure in the goblin caves, widened over centuries by the Blackfang clan to serve as a gateway to their deeper tunnels. description.description: What the player sees, hears and smells standing in this place right now. Describe THIS place only -- not what neighbours it, not what is visible out of a window or across the way, because the world around it can move. Second person. One paragraph, 4 to 6 sentences.

lore.description: What this place is, who made it and what happened here. Written for the game engine rather than the player. One paragraph, 3 to 5 sentences.

name.description: What this room is called -- ONLY when the instructions above ask you to name it. Leave this out entirely otherwise. A short noun phrase a player would type to walk into it, carrying the article English wants on it: "the counting room". Never the name of the building it is in, never a name this story has already given to a room, a person or a thing, and never a comma.

items.description: Portable things lying loose in this place that a player could pick up and carry away. Empty is the right answer for most rooms.

name.description: What the thing is called, as a player would type it to pick it up. A short noun phrase, 1 to 4 words, lower case unless it is a proper name. Never the name of a person or of a place.

description.description: What it is and what state it is in, consistent with the description of the room you just wrote. One or two sentences.

use_kind.description: The engine's physical profile: ordinary unless it is food, a drink, a healing dose, a firestarter, a prying lever, lockpicks, or a key. Choose healing only for an actual restorative dose allowed by this world. Profiles supply behavior from code, never from the description.

combustible.description: True only if this portable thing can be destroyed by an ordinary carried firestarter: dry paper, cloth or wood. False for stone, metal, liquids, or anything uncertain.

readable.description: True only if this thing has WRITING on it that a player could read: a note, a letter, a label, a docket, a page, a sign, an inscription. False for everything else, which is most things.

inscription.description: The words written on it, exactly as they appear, and only when `readable` is true. Write what is actually on the thing -- what a player would read off it -- not a description of it. A few words, a line, or a few short lines; well under the limit, and finished rather than trailing off. Leave this out entirely when nothing is written on it.

people.description: The person who is in this place right now. Write the one the instructions describe.

fullname.description: Their full name, as a player would type it to speak to them. 2 or 3 words.

nickname.description: What they are called to their face. 1 or 2 words.

appearance.description: What somebody walking in sees of them, consistent with the room you just wrote and with the race and age you were given for them. One or two sentences.

personality.description: How they behave and how they treat a stranger. One or two sentences.

backstory.description: Why they are in this place and what they want. Third person, by name. Two or three sentences.

likes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they enjoy.

dislikes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they cannot stand.

fears.description: A comma separated list of 1 or 2 things they are afraid of.

conscious_desire.description: What this person would say if somebody asked them what they want, today, in this story. Specific, and reachable by somebody standing in a room in this world. Name something to move TOWARD, never something to stop or escape. One sentence, third person, by name.

unconscious_desire.description: What they are actually pursuing and would deny if you said it to them. It sits at an angle to the conscious desire rather than agreeing with it: the conscious desire is the reason they give themselves, and this is what keeps them going when that reason runs out. One sentence, third person, by name.

recognized_need.description: Something they know they must do whether they want to or not, and may resent. A real obligation this world imposes on them -- their work, their family, their debt, their oath, their body -- and one that can get in the way of the conscious desire. One sentence, third person, by name.

unrecognized_need.description: What they need and cannot see, not even unconsciously. A reader should be able to see it from the backstory above while they cannot. If they never do it, pursuing the conscious desire ruins them. It must not be the conscious desire said twice. One sentence, third person, by name.

desire_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the CONSCIOUS DESIRE has -- the one that fits the act they would take tomorrow morning.

need_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the UNRECOGNIZED NEED has. It may be the same label as the one above; the more interesting answer is usually a different one.

detail.description: You stand on the ashen slope of the Spire, where the wind carries the acrid tang of burning pitch and the faint metallic bite of the river below. The cave mouth yawns behind you, its edges jagged with obsidian, while ahead the land falls away in a steep, rocky descent. The ground is littered with charred scraps of wood and the occasional glint of iron ore, half-buried in the soot. The air hums with the low, almost imperceptible pulse of a ley line, detectable only by the faint vibration in the iron of your armor. A lone figure crouches near a smoldering patch of earth, their silhouette sharp against the dim glow of the setting sun.
detail.lore: This is the outer slope of the Ashen Spire, a dead volcano repurposed by the Church of the Eternal Pyre as a site for heretic burnings. The ground is rich with iron deposits, and the ley lines here are strong but unstable, often flickering in and out of detectability. The Veythi use this area as a meeting point for their black-market dealings, taking advantage of the Church’s reluctance to patrol too close to the goblin caves. The wind carries the scent of the river Veyth, its iron-laden waters undrinkable but vital for the forges of Durnhold.

people.personality: Ryn speaks in a low, measured voice, their words deliberate but not unkind. They have a dry wit and little patience for fools, but they respect competence and directness.
people.backstory: Ryn Veyth has spent decades trading along the river Veyth, smuggling goods between Durnhold and the goblin territories. They know the Spire’s slopes well, using them as a neutral ground for deals too risky for the Rust Market. Lately, they’ve been tracking rumors of a Durnish noble lost in the caves, hoping to turn the information into coin or favor.
people.likes: bargaining, river mist, sharp blades
people.conscious_desire: Ryn wants to sell the location of the prince to the highest bidder before the Church finds out they know.
people.unconscious_desire: Ryn wants to prove they are more than just a smuggler, that their knowledge has weight beyond the river’s edge.
people.recognized_need: Ryn must keep their deals secret from the Church, or face the pyre for heresy.
people.unrecognized_need: Ryn needs to trust someone with the truth, or the weight of their secrets will drown them.

prompts.detail:
## Universe Details
physics: Gravity is consistent at 9.8 m/s², but the world is veined with ley lines—thin, invisible rivers of latent magic that pulse at a frequency of 0.3 Hz, detectable only by iron-forged compasses. These lines can be tapped by blood rituals, but each use drains the caster’s lifespan by exactly one day per minute of magic. The ley lines are finite; overuse in a region causes them to fade for a century. No magic can resurrect the dead or heal mortal wounds, only delay them.
technology: The world is locked in a late medieval stasis, with iron and steel as the primary metals. Clockwork mechanisms exist but are rare, limited to devices no larger than a loaf of bread due to the scarcity of precision gears. Gunpowder is known but unstable, often exploding prematurely in 1 out of 5 attempts. Most advancements are suppressed by the Church of the Eternal Pyre, which burns any invention deemed heretical.
geographies: The kingdom of Durnhold is a land of jagged iron cliffs and black pine forests, its heart dominated by the Ashen Spire, a dead volcano where the Church burns heretics. The goblin caves lie beneath the Spire’s roots, a labyrinth of obsidian tunnels lit by bioluminescent fungi that dim every 12 hours. The nearest town, Hollow’s End, is a day’s ride north, its walls built from the bones of ancient trolls. The river Veyth, wide and slow, marks the border between Durnhold and the goblin territories, its waters undrinkable due to high iron content.
races: Durnish, Goblins, Trollkin, Veythi
civilizations: The Kingdom of Durnhold is ruled by the Iron Council, a cabal of knights and priests who enforce the Church’s decrees from the Obsidian Throne in the capital, Spire’s Rest. The goblins are divided into warring clans, the largest being the Blackfang, who control the dungeon where the prince is held. The Trollkin have no settlements, only nomadic bands, while the Veythi operate from floating barges on the river, their only permanent structure being the Rust Market, a black-market hub hidden in the river’s mist. The uneasy peace is maintained by the Iron Council’s threat of annihilation and the goblins’ fear of open war, but raids and executions are common.


## Story Details
title: The Iron Gate Descends
genre: dark fantasy
preface: The iron gate groans as it settles into the stone, its teeth biting into the threshold with a finality that echoes through the cavern. You stand in the dim glow of bioluminescent fungi, the air thick with the scent of damp earth and old blood. Your gauntleted hand rests on the hilt of your Veldarian sword, its edge still sharp despite the weight of the blackened plate armor pressing into your shoulders. The prince’s signet ring, cold in your palm, was found in the mud outside this gate—proof he passed this way. Behind you, the tunnel slopes upward, but the way forward is a yawning maw of obsidian, the walls slick with moisture. Somewhere in the dark, something skitters.
summary: A Durnish knight, clad in heavy blackened plate, stands at the threshold of the goblin caves beneath the Ashen Spire, having just forced open an iron gate. The prince’s signet ring, discovered in the mud, confirms his passage into the tunnels. The air is thick with the scent of damp earth and the faint glow of fungi, while the distant sound of movement hints at unseen dangers ahead. The Church’s decree to retrieve the prince or die trying weighs heavily, but the immediate threat is the darkness itself.


## The Place
name: surface
teaser: The mouth of the cave opens to the ashen slopes of the Spire, where the wind carries the scent of burning pitch.

## Instructions
Write this place out in full.
- The description is what the player reads on arrival. Address them as "you"
- Describe what is here now, not the history -- the history is the lore
- Stay consistent with the universe and with the teaser above
- Respect the stated length of each field

## What Is Lying Here
List AT MOST 3 portable things a player could pick up and carry away.
- Nothing is the right answer for most rooms. An empty list is a complete answer
- Only loose, portable things. Not the door, not the floor, not the machinery
  bolted to it -- something a person could put in a pocket or under an arm
- Each one must be consistent with the description you just wrote, and worth
  the player noticing
- Pick its use_kind from the supplied physical profiles. Ordinary is the
  default. Food and drink can be consumed without healing; healing is only
  a restorative dose this world permits. Firestarters burn combustible
  objects, levers pry jammed passages, lockpicks try locks, and a key only
  opens a passage explicitly matched to it. Mark combustible only when an
  ordinary firestarter can destroy the object. The engine owns the effects
  and their amounts; its description cannot grant extra powers
- If a thing has WRITING on it -- a note, a letter, a handbill, a label, a
  docket, a page, a sign -- mark it readable and WRITE OUT WHAT IS WRITTEN
  ON IT, exactly as it appears on the thing. The words themselves, not a
  description of them, and short enough to finish -- a few words, a line,
  or a few short lines. The game keeps those words and a player reading it
  twice reads the same ones
- Never name it after a person or after a place. Already spoken for in this story, so do not reuse: Veythra the Silent, iron key, prince's signet ring, damp scroll, iron shard, rusted dagger, tattered cloth

## Who Is Here
Write EXACTLY 1 person who is in this place right now.
- Anyone you write is somebody the player can walk up to and talk to, so they
  have to have a reason to be standing here and something they want
- Do not write the player, and do not write somebody passing through
- Never give them the name of a place, of a thing, or any name already
  spoken for above

Who they are is already decided. Write these people and do not change them:
  the 1st is Veythi, about 52, non-binary

## Their Four Objects of Desire

Write four things this person is after and pick two labels for them. Work from
everything above -- their backstory, what they like and dislike, what they are
afraid of, how old they are, how strong their will is, and where they are
standing.

The two labels are picked from this list and nothing else:

  keep     They are holding on to something they already have.
  obtain   They are trying to get hold of something they do not have.
  reach    They are trying to get to a particular place.
  attend   They are trying to stay near a particular person.
  avoid    They are trying to get away from a person or a place.
  withhold They are trying to stop somebody else getting something.
  offer    They are trying to put something into somebody else's hands.

Rules:
- Every one of the four names something to move TOWARD. A field that only says
  what they want to stop or escape is not finished. Say what is on the other
  side of it.
- Write them so an ordinary act in a room could serve one: picking something
  up, handing something over, walking out, staying put, standing near
  somebody. Do not write a desire nobody could act on in a room.
- Keep them consistent with the fears and dislikes above. A fear is usually the
  shadow of one of these four and should read that way.
- The conscious desire and the unrecognized need must not be the same thing
  said twice.
- Write in the third person, by name.
- Do not resolve any of them, and do not say how the story ends.
- Respect the stated length of each field.

description.description: What the player sees, hears and smells standing in this place right now. Describe THIS place only -- not what neighbours it, not what is visible out of a window or across the way, because the world around it can move. Second person. One paragraph, 4 to 6 sentences.

lore.description: What this place is, who made it and what happened here. Written for the game engine rather than the player. One paragraph, 3 to 5 sentences.

name.description: What this room is called -- ONLY when the instructions above ask you to name it. Leave this out entirely otherwise. items.description: Portable things lying loose in this place that a player could pick up and carry away. Empty is the right answer for most rooms.

name.description: What the thing is called, as a player would type it to pick it up. A short noun phrase, 1 to 4 words, lower case unless it is a proper name. Never the name of a person or of a place.

description.description: What it is and what state it is in, consistent with the description of the room you just wrote. One or two sentences.

combustible.description: True only if this portable thing can be destroyed by an ordinary carried firestarter: dry paper, cloth or wood. False for stone, metal, liquids, or anything uncertain.

readable.description: True only if this thing has WRITING on it that a player could read: a note, a letter, a label, a docket, a page, a sign, an inscription. False for everything else, which is most things.

inscription.description: The words written on it, exactly as they appear, and only when `readable` is true. people.description: People who are in this place right now.

fullname.description: Their full name, as a player would type it to speak to them. 2 or 3 words.

nickname.description: What they are called to their face. 1 or 2 words.

appearance.description: What somebody walking in sees of them, consistent with the room you just wrote and with the race and age you were given for them. One or two sentences.

personality.description: How they behave and how they treat a stranger. One or two sentences.

backstory.description: Why they are in this place and what they want. Third person, by name. Two or three sentences.

likes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they enjoy.

dislikes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they cannot stand.

fears.description: A comma separated list of 1 or 2 things they are afraid of.

conscious_desire.description: What this person would say if somebody asked them what they want, today, in this story. Specific, and reachable by somebody standing in a room in this world. Name something to move TOWARD, never something to stop or escape. One sentence, third person, by name.

unconscious_desire.description: What they are actually pursuing and would deny if you said it to them. It sits at an angle to the conscious desire rather than agreeing with it: the conscious desire is the reason they give themselves, and this is what keeps them going when that reason runs out. One sentence, third person, by name.

recognized_need.description: Something they know they must do whether they want to or not, and may resent. A real obligation this world imposes on them -- their work, their family, their debt, their oath, their body -- and one that can get in the way of the conscious desire. One sentence, third person, by name.

unrecognized_need.description: What they need and cannot see, not even unconsciously. A reader should be able to see it from the backstory above while they cannot. desire_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the CONSCIOUS DESIRE has -- the one that fits the act they would take tomorrow morning.

need_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the UNRECOGNIZED NEED has. It may be the same label as the one above; the more interesting answer is usually a different one.

history.content:
## Universe Details
physics: Gravity is consistent at 9.8 m/s², but the world is veined with ley lines—thin, invisible rivers of latent magic that pulse at a frequency of 0.3 Hz, detectable only by iron-forged compasses. These lines can be tapped by blood rituals, but each use drains the caster’s lifespan by exactly one day per minute of magic. The ley lines are finite; overuse in a region causes them to fade for a century. No magic can resurrect the dead or heal mortal wounds, only delay them.
technology: The world is locked in a late medieval stasis, with iron and steel as the primary metals. Clockwork mechanisms exist but are rare, limited to devices no larger than a loaf of bread due to the scarcity of precision gears. Gunpowder is known but unstable, often exploding prematurely in 1 out of 5 attempts. Most advancements are suppressed by the Church of the Eternal Pyre, which burns any invention deemed heretical.
geographies: The kingdom of Durnhold is a land of jagged iron cliffs and black pine forests, its heart dominated by the Ashen Spire, a dead volcano where the Church burns heretics. The goblin caves lie beneath the Spire’s roots, a labyrinth of obsidian tunnels lit by bioluminescent fungi that dim every 12 hours. The nearest town, Hollow’s End, is a day’s ride north, its walls built from the bones of ancient trolls. The river Veyth, wide and slow, marks the border between Durnhold and the goblin territories, its waters undrinkable due to high iron content.
races: Durnish, Goblins, Trollkin, Veythi
civilizations: The Kingdom of Durnhold is ruled by the Iron Council, a cabal of knights and priests who enforce the Church’s decrees from the Obsidian Throne in the capital, Spire’s Rest. The goblins are divided into warring clans, the largest being the Blackfang, who control the dungeon where the prince is held. The Trollkin have no settlements, only nomadic bands, while the Veythi operate from floating barges on the river, their only permanent structure being the Rust Market, a black-market hub hidden in the river’s mist. The uneasy peace is maintained by the Iron Council’s threat of annihilation and the goblins’ fear of open war, but raids and executions are common.


## Story Details
title: The Iron Gate Descends
genre: dark fantasy
preface: The iron gate groans as it settles into the stone, its teeth biting into the threshold with a finality that echoes through the cavern. You stand in the dim glow of bioluminescent fungi, the air thick with the scent of damp earth and old blood. Your gauntleted hand rests on the hilt of your Veldarian sword, its edge still sharp despite the weight of the blackened plate armor pressing into your shoulders. The prince’s signet ring, cold in your palm, was found in the mud outside this gate—proof he passed this way. Behind you, the tunnel slopes upward, but the way forward is a yawning maw of obsidian, the walls slick with moisture. Somewhere in the dark, something skitters.
summary: A Durnish knight, clad in heavy blackened plate, stands at the threshold of the goblin caves beneath the Ashen Spire, having just forced open an iron gate. The prince’s signet ring, discovered in the mud, confirms his passage into the tunnels. The air is thick with the scent of damp earth and the faint glow of fungi, while the distant sound of movement hints at unseen dangers ahead. The Church’s decree to retrieve the prince or die trying weighs heavily, but the immediate threat is the darkness itself.

detail.description: You stand at the edge of Hollow’s End, the troll-bone walls rising like jagged teeth against the bruised twilight sky. The air carries the sharp tang of iron from the river Veyth and the damp rot of black pine needles underfoot. The gate, a massive slab of iron-bound oak, yawns open, its hinges groaning in the wind. A single lantern flickers on a post, casting long shadows across the packed earth of the road. The scent of woodsmoke lingers, though no fires burn in sight.
detail.lore: Hollow’s End was built from the bones of ancient trolls, a grim testament to Durnhold’s victories over the Trollkin. The town serves as the last outpost before the goblin caves and the Ashen Spire, a place where travelers and mercenaries gather before venturing into the wilds. The Iron Council maintains a loose grip here, allowing the Rust Market’s black trade to thrive in the shadows. The walls, though imposing, are more for show than defense, as the true danger lies beyond them.

description.description: What the player sees, hears and smells standing in this place right now. Describe THIS place only -- not what neighbours it, not what is visible out of a window or across the way, because the world around it can move. Second person. One paragraph, 4 to 6 sentences.

lore.description: What this place is, who made it and what happened here. Written for the game engine rather than the player. One paragraph, 3 to 5 sentences.

name.description: What this room is called -- ONLY when the instructions above ask you to name it. Leave this out entirely otherwise. A short noun phrase a player would type to walk into it, carrying the article English wants on it: "the counting room". Never the name of the building it is in, never a name this story has already given to a room, a person or a thing, and never a comma.

items.description: Portable things lying loose in this place that a player could pick up and carry away. Empty is the right answer for most rooms.

name.description: What the thing is called, as a player would type it to pick it up. A short noun phrase, 1 to 4 words, lower case unless it is a proper name. Never the name of a person or of a place.

description.description: What it is and what state it is in, consistent with the description of the room you just wrote. One or two sentences.

use_kind.description: The engine's physical profile: ordinary unless it is food, a drink, a healing dose, a firestarter, a prying lever, lockpicks, or a key. Choose healing only for an actual restorative dose allowed by this world. Profiles supply behavior from code, never from the description.

combustible.description: True only if this portable thing can be destroyed by an ordinary carried firestarter: dry paper, cloth or wood. False for stone, metal, liquids, or anything uncertain.

readable.description: True only if this thing has WRITING on it that a player could read: a note, a letter, a label, a docket, a page, a sign, an inscription. False for everything else, which is most things.

inscription.description: The words written on it, exactly as they appear, and only when `readable` is true. Write what is actually on the thing -- what a player would read off it -- not a description of it. A few words, a line, or a few short lines; well under the limit, and finished rather than trailing off. Leave this out entirely when nothing is written on it.

people.description: The 2 people who are in this place right now. Write all 2 the instructions describe, in the order they are given there.

fullname.description: Their full name, as a player would type it to speak to them. 2 or 3 words.

nickname.description: What they are called to their face. 1 or 2 words.

appearance.description: What somebody walking in sees of them, consistent with the room you just wrote and with the race and age you were given for them. One or two sentences.

personality.description: How they behave and how they treat a stranger. One or two sentences.

backstory.description: Why they are in this place and what they want. Third person, by name. Two or three sentences.

likes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they enjoy.

dislikes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they cannot stand.

fears.description: A comma separated list of 1 or 2 things they are afraid of.

conscious_desire.description: What this person would say if somebody asked them what they want, today, in this story. Specific, and reachable by somebody standing in a room in this world. Name something to move TOWARD, never something to stop or escape. One sentence, third person, by name.

unconscious_desire.description: What they are actually pursuing and would deny if you said it to them. It sits at an angle to the conscious desire rather than agreeing with it: the conscious desire is the reason they give themselves, and this is what keeps them going when that reason runs out. One sentence, third person, by name.

recognized_need.description: Something they know they must do whether they want to or not, and may resent. A real obligation this world imposes on them -- their work, their family, their debt, their oath, their body -- and one that can get in the way of the conscious desire. One sentence, third person, by name.

unrecognized_need.description: What they need and cannot see, not even unconsciously. A reader should be able to see it from the backstory above while they cannot. If they never do it, pursuing the conscious desire ruins them. It must not be the conscious desire said twice. One sentence, third person, by name.

desire_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the CONSCIOUS DESIRE has -- the one that fits the act they would take tomorrow morning.

need_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the UNRECOGNIZED NEED has. It may be the same label as the one above; the more interesting answer is usually a different one.

technology: The world is locked in a late medieval stasis, with iron and steel as the primary metals. Clockwork mechanisms exist but are rare, limited to devices no larger than a loaf of bread due to the scarcity of precision gears. Gunpowder is known but unstable, often exploding prematurely in 1 out of 5 attempts. Most advancements are suppressed by the Church of the Eternal Pyre, which burns any invention deemed heretical.
geographies: The kingdom of Durnhold is a land of jagged iron cliffs and black pine forests, its heart dominated by the Ashen Spire, a dead volcano where the Church burns heretics. The nearest town, Hollow’s End, is a day’s ride north, its walls built from the bones of ancient trolls. detail.lore: Spire’s Rest is the capital of Durnhold, built around the base of the Ashen Spire, a dead volcano repurposed as the seat of the Iron Council. The city’s iron walls were forged from the same ore mined from the Spire’s depths, and its towers serve as both watchposts and execution sites for the Church’s heretics. The streets are a maze of smithies, barracks, and temples, all under the ever-watchful gaze of the Obsidian Throne. The city’s wealth flows from the iron trade, but its true power lies in the fear it instills in those who dare defy the Church.

people.appearance: A towering Trollkin with weathered gray skin and a long, braided mane of black hair streaked with silver. Their massive frame is wrapped in a tattered cloak of stitched hides, and a single iron ring pierces their left eyebrow, glinting in the fading light.
people.personality: Rask speaks in a low, rumbling voice, their words deliberate and heavy with the weight of years. They treat strangers with cautious respect, though their patience wears thin with those who waste time or speak in riddles.
people.backstory: Rask once served as a mercenary for the Iron Council, but after witnessing the execution of an innocent family, they abandoned their post and now wander the fringes of Durnhold. They seek redemption but know the Church will never grant it. The signet ring of a fallen noble, found in the mud outside the goblin caves, has drawn them here, though they refuse to say why.
people.likes: honest deals, quiet nights, the taste of roasted venison
people.dislikes: liars, the Church’s pyres, the smell of burning flesh
people.conscious_desire: Rask wants to uncover the truth behind the prince’s disappearance, no matter the cost.
people.unconscious_desire: Rask wants to prove that even a monster like them can still do what is right.
people.recognized_need: Rask must avoid drawing the attention of the Iron Council, or they will be hunted as a deserter.
people.unrecognized_need: Rask needs to let go of the guilt that binds them to the past.

people.appearance: A wiry goblin woman with leathery green skin and sharp, yellowed teeth. Her black hair is tied back in a tight braid, and her dark eyes dart constantly, as if expecting an ambush. She wears a patched leather vest over a tunic of faded red, and a belt of small, rusted knives hangs at her hip.
people.personality: Mira is quick to speak and quicker to laugh, though her humor often carries a bite. She treats strangers with a mix of curiosity and suspicion, always sizing them up for potential gain or threat.
people.backstory: Mira is a scout for the Blackfang clan, sent to Spire’s Rest under the guise of a merchant to gather intelligence. She knows the prince was taken into the goblin caves, and she intends to use that knowledge to bargain for her clan’s safety. But the Iron Council’s spies are everywhere, and one wrong move could see her burned as a heretic.
people.likes: shiny trinkets, clever bargains, the thrill of a good chase
people.dislikes: the Church’s inquisitors, being watched, the taste of iron
people.conscious_desire: Mira wants to trade the prince’s location for her clan’s freedom from the Iron Council’s raids.
people.unconscious_desire: Mira wants to outsmart the Church and prove that even a goblin can outmaneuver the mighty.
people.recognized_need: Mira must avoid being recognized as a spy, or she will be executed on the spot.
people.unrecognized_need: Mira needs to trust someone, or she will die alone in a world that hates her kind.

The fungi here are a symbiotic growth, fed by the decay of the warren’s many victims, their glow dimming in sync with the ley lines’ pulse. The Iron Council has long suspected the prince was taken here, but none who entered the warren have returned to confirm it.

## Universe Details
physics: Ordinary physics, and a tide that keeps to its table.
technology: Rope, tar, lamp oil and a ledger.
geographies: One quay, one custom house standing on it, and the water at the end of both.
races: Harbourfolk
civilizations: A port that has never been anything else.


## Story Details
title: The Quay House
genre: harbour mystery
preface: The custom house has been locked since noon and the seal on the door is broken.
summary: Somebody was inside the custom house when the whole quay says it was empty.


## The Place
name: The Custom House room 1
teaser: A room inside The Custom House, 7 by 4 paces on storey 0.
## Where This Room Is
The game's own records of this room, already decided and not yours to
change. Write the room around them: do not contradict a measurement, and
do not give it a way out this list does not have.
This room is 7 by 4 paces -- about 11 by 6 metres. It is on storey 0 of The Custom House, which is 14 by 10 paces across; storey 0 is the ground floor. Its ways out: a door in the east wall, to The Custom House room 2; a stair up to The Custom House room 5, on storey 1; a way out to The Quay, which is outside The Custom House. Those are every way out of this room.
## Instructions
Write this place out in full.
- The description is what the player reads on arrival. Address them as "you"
- Describe what is here now, not the history -- the history is the lore
- Stay consistent with the universe and with the teaser above
- Respect the stated length of each field
- NAME THIS ROOM. It is one room inside The Custom House. The player reads the room and
  the place together -- "the <your name> of The Custom House" -- so name the ROOM only,
  and never put the place's own name into it. A short noun phrase carrying the
  article English wants on it, 2 to 4 words: "the counting room", "the cold
  store", "the harbourmaster's office". Name it for what the floor plan above
  says this room is and for what you have just described standing in it. Never
  a comma in it

## What Is Lying Here
List AT MOST 3 portable things a player could pick up and carry away.
- Nothing is the right answer for most rooms. An empty list is a complete answer
- Only loose, portable things. Not the door, not the floor, not the machinery
  bolted to it -- something a person could put in a pocket or under an arm
- Each one must be consistent with the description you just wrote, and worth
  the player noticing
- Pick its use_kind from the supplied physical profiles. Ordinary is the
  default. Food and drink can be consumed without healing; healing is only
  a restorative dose this world permits. Firestarters burn combustible
  objects, levers pry jammed passages, lockpicks try locks, and a key only
  opens a passage explicitly matched to it. Mark combustible only when an
  ordinary firestarter can destroy the object. The engine owns the effects
  and their amounts; its description cannot grant extra powers
- If a thing has WRITING on it -- a note, a letter, a handbill, a label, a
  docket, a page, a sign -- mark it readable and WRITE OUT WHAT IS WRITTEN
  ON IT, exactly as it appears on the thing. The words themselves, not a
  description of them, and short enough to finish -- a few words, a line,
  or a few short lines. The game keeps those words and a player reading it
  twice reads the same ones
- Never name it after a person or after a place. Already spoken for in this story, so do not reuse: Nell Cawsand

## Who Is Here
Write EXACTLY 2 people who are in this place right now.
- Anyone you write is somebody the player can walk up to and talk to, so they
  have to have a reason to be standing here and something they want
- Do not write the player, and do not write somebody passing through
- Never give them the name of a place, of a thing, or any name already
  spoken for above

Who they are is already decided. Write these people and do not change them:
  the 1st is Harbourfolk, about 61, trans man
  the 2nd is Harbourfolk, about 63, trans man

## Their Four Objects of Desire

Write four things this person is after and pick two labels for them. Work from
everything above -- their backstory, what they like and dislike, what they are
afraid of, how old they are, how strong their will is, and where they are
standing.

The two labels are picked from this list and nothing else:

  keep     They are holding on to something they already have.
  obtain   They are trying to get hold of something they do not have.
  reach    They are trying to get to a particular place.
  attend   They are trying to stay near a particular person.
  avoid    They are trying to get away from a person or a place.
  withhold They are trying to stop somebody else getting something.
  offer    They are trying to put something into somebody else's hands.

Rules:
- Every one of the four names something to move TOWARD. A field that only says
  what they want to stop or escape is not finished. Say what is on the other
  side of it.
- Write them so an ordinary act in a room could serve one: picking something
  up, handing something over, walking out, staying put, standing near
  somebody. Do not write a desire nobody could act on in a room.
- Keep them consistent with the fears and dislikes above. A fear is usually the
  shadow of one of these four and should read that way.
- The conscious desire and the unrecognized need must not be the same thing
  said twice.
- Write in the third person, by name.
- Do not resolve any of them, and do not say how the story ends.
- Respect the stated length of each field.
- Each person in this room gets their own four. Two people in one room must not
  want the same thing in the same words.
- At least one of them should want something that is in this room or one step
  out of it.

description.description: What the player sees, hears and smells standing in this place right now. Describe THIS place only -- not what neighbours it, not what is visible out of a window or across the way, because the world around it can move. Second person. One paragraph, 4 to 6 sentences.

lore.description: What this place is, who made it and what happened here. Written for the game engine rather than the player. One paragraph, 3 to 5 sentences.

name.description: What this room is called -- ONLY when the instructions above ask you to name it. Leave this out entirely otherwise. A short noun phrase a player would type to walk into it, carrying the article English wants on it: "the counting room". Never the name of the building it is in, never a name this story has already given to a room, a person or a thing, and never a comma.

items.description: Portable things lying loose in this place that a player could pick up and carry away. Empty is the right answer for most rooms.

name.description: What the thing is called, as a player would type it to pick it up. A short noun phrase, 1 to 4 words, lower case unless it is a proper name. Never the name of a person or of a place.

description.description: What it is and what state it is in, consistent with the description of the room you just wrote. One or two sentences.

use_kind.description: The engine's physical profile: ordinary unless it is food, a drink, a healing dose, a firestarter, a prying lever, lockpicks, or a key. Choose healing only for an actual restorative dose allowed by this world. Profiles supply behavior from code, never from the description.

combustible.description: True only if this portable thing can be destroyed by an ordinary carried firestarter: dry paper, cloth or wood. False for stone, metal, liquids, or anything uncertain.

readable.description: True only if this thing has WRITING on it that a player could read: a note, a letter, a label, a docket, a page, a sign, an inscription. False for everything else, which is most things.

inscription.description: The words written on it, exactly as they appear, and only when `readable` is true. Write what is actually on the thing -- what a player would read off it -- not a description of it. A few words, a line, or a few short lines; well under the limit, and finished rather than trailing off. Leave this out entirely when nothing is written on it.

people.description: The 2 people who are in this place right now. Write all 2 the instructions describe, in the order they are given there.

fullname.description: Their full name, as a player would type it to speak to them. 2 or 3 words.

nickname.description: What they are called to their face. 1 or 2 words.

appearance.description: What somebody walking in sees of them, consistent with the room you just wrote and with the race and age you were given for them. One or two sentences.

personality.description: How they behave and how they treat a stranger. One or two sentences.

backstory.description: Why they are in this place and what they want. Third person, by name. Two or three sentences.

likes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they enjoy.

dislikes.description: A comma separated list of 2 or 3 things they cannot stand.

fears.description: A comma separated list of 1 or 2 things they are afraid of.

conscious_desire.description: What this person would say if somebody asked them what they want, today, in this story. Specific, and reachable by somebody standing in a room in this world. Name something to move TOWARD, never something to stop or escape. One sentence, third person, by name.

unconscious_desire.description: What they are actually pursuing and would deny if you said it to them. It sits at an angle to the conscious desire rather than agreeing with it: the conscious desire is the reason they give themselves, and this is what keeps them going when that reason runs out. One sentence, third person, by name.

recognized_need.description: Something they know they must do whether they want to or not, and may resent. A real obligation this world imposes on them -- their work, their family, their debt, their oath, their body -- and one that can get in the way of the conscious desire. One sentence, third person, by name.

unrecognized_need.description: What they need and cannot see, not even unconsciously. A reader should be able to see it from the backstory above while they cannot. If they never do it, pursuing the conscious desire ruins them. It must not be the conscious desire said twice. One sentence, third person, by name.

desire_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the CONSCIOUS DESIRE has -- the one that fits the act they would take tomorrow morning.

need_pursuit.description: Which listed shape the UNRECOGNIZED NEED has. It may be the same label as the one above; the more interesting answer is usually a different one.

detail.description: You stand in a dim, square chamber where the scent of salt and old paper lingers thick in the air. The floorboards creak underfoot, worn smooth by decades of boots, and a single oil lamp flickers on a scarred wooden desk, casting long shadows across the walls. A heavy door to the east bears fresh scratches around its broken seal, and a narrow staircase spirals upward in the corner. The way out to the quay yawns open behind you, letting in the damp breeze from the water.
detail.lore: This is the ground-floor receiving room of the Custom House, where ledgers were once checked and duties collected from every ship that docked. Built a century ago when the port was young, it has seen generations of harbourfolk pass through its doors, though today it stands unusually quiet. The broken seal suggests someone entered after hours, and the lamp left burning hints at haste.
detail.name: the receiving room

items.name: broken seal
items.description: A wax seal, snapped in two, its edges jagged where it was torn from the door. The red wax is still soft in places.

items.name: oil lamp
items.description: A brass lamp with a glass chimney, half-full of oil and still lit. The wick smolders steadily.

people.appearance: A broad-shouldered harbourfolk with silver-streaked hair tied back in a short queue, his face lined with years of squinting into the wind. He wears a faded waistcoat over a once-white shirt, the sleeves rolled to his elbows.
people.personality: Gruff but precise, Tobias speaks in clipped sentences and expects the same in return. He has little patience for nonsense but a sharp eye for detail.
people.backstory: Tobias has worked the Custom House for forty years, first as a clerk and now as its unofficial caretaker. He was the last to lock up yesterday, and the broken seal has left him unsettled. He knows every ledger by heart and resents the idea that someone might have tampered with them.
people.likes: order, quiet, strong tea
people.fears: being blamed for a mistake, losing his position
people.conscious_desire: Tobias wants to find out who broke the seal and restore the room to its proper state.
people.unconscious_desire: Tobias wants to prove he is still the one person who can keep the Custom House running as it should.
people.recognized_need: Tobias must report the broken seal to the harbourmaster, whether he wants to or not.
people.unrecognized_need: Tobias needs to accept that the Custom House may no longer need him as it once did.

people.appearance: Tall and lean, Elias moves with the deliberate slowness of someone who has spent a lifetime measuring cargo. His hands are ink-stained, and his coat, though threadbare, is always buttoned to the collar.
people.personality: Elias is methodical to the point of obsession, speaking in a low, measured tone. He trusts numbers more than people and treats every discrepancy like a personal insult.
people.backstory: Elias was the Custom House’s head accountant until his eyesight began to fail, forcing him into early retirement. He still visits daily, unable to let go of the ledgers he once kept. The broken seal has drawn him here, convinced it hides an error he missed.
people.likes: precision, old books, the smell of ink
people.conscious_desire: Elias wants to examine the ledgers to ensure no entries were altered during the break-in.
people.unconscious_desire: Elias wants to be the one who uncovers the truth, proving he is still indispensable.
people.recognized_need: Elias must admit that his eyes can no longer read the smallest print in the ledgers.
people.unrecognized_need: Elias needs to teach someone else the work before it is lost forever.

detail.description: You stand in a dim, windowless chamber where the air carries the sharp tang of ink and the faint salt of the quay outside. A single oil lamp flickers on a heavy oak desk, casting long shadows over scattered ledgers and a broken wax seal lying near the edge. The stone walls are bare except for a few rusted hooks, and the floorboards creak underfoot, worn smooth by decades of footsteps. The only sounds are the distant lapping of water against the quay and the soft rustle of paper shifting in the draft.
detail.lore: This was once the ledger room of the custom house, where harbourfolk recorded the comings and goings of every ship and cargo. The desk and hooks were installed by the first harbourmaster, and the floorboards have never been replaced. The broken seal suggests someone forced their way in recently, though the ledgers themselves appear undisturbed.

items.name: broken wax seal
items.description: A shattered red wax seal, its edges jagged where it was pried apart. It lies near the edge of the desk, its fragments still clinging to a scrap of parchment.

items.name: oil lamp
items.description: A brass lamp filled with oil, its wick burning low but steady. The glass chimney is smudged with soot.

people.appearance: A tall Harbourfolk woman with silver-streaked black hair tied back in a tight braid. She wears a faded blue coat over a practical linen shirt, her hands ink-stained from years of ledger work.
people.personality: Mara speaks with quiet authority, her voice steady but weary, as if she has spent a lifetime explaining things to people who refuse to listen. She is patient with those who show respect for the work, but her patience thins quickly with carelessness.
people.backstory: Mara has been the head ledger-keeper of the custom house for thirty years, a role she inherited from her father. She was the last to lock the building at noon, and she knows every inch of its records. The broken seal has shaken her; she cannot recall a time the custom house was breached.
people.likes: order, quiet, well-kept ledgers
people.fears: being blamed for the breach, losing her position
people.conscious_desire: Mara wants to restore the seal and prove the ledgers were untouched.
people.unconscious_desire: Mara wants to uncover who broke in, even if it means admitting the custom house was vulnerable.
people.recognized_need: Mara must report the breach to the harbourmaster, no matter the personal cost.
people.unrecognized_need: Mara needs to trust that someone else can share the burden of keeping the records safe.

people.appearance: A wiry young Harbourfolk woman with sun-browned skin and a mop of curly auburn hair. She wears a patched apron over her simple dress, her sleeves rolled up to her elbows, revealing arms marked with faint scars from rope burns.
people.personality: Tess is quick to laugh and quicker to act, her energy restless as the tide. She speaks in bursts, her words tumbling over each other, and she has little patience for hesitation or secrecy.
people.backstory: Tess is an apprentice to the harbourmaster, sent to fetch a ledger for an urgent inspection. She arrived just after noon to find the door sealed and the wax broken, and she has been waiting inside ever since, unsure what to do.
people.likes: adventure, the smell of the docks, solving puzzles
people.fears: failing her master, being trapped in small spaces
people.conscious_desire: Tess wants to find the ledger she was sent for and leave before anyone notices she was here.
people.unconscious_desire: Tess wants to prove she is more than just an errand runner, even if it means overstepping.
people.recognized_need: Tess must deliver the ledger to the harbourmaster by sunset, no matter what.
people.unrecognized_need: Tess needs to learn when to ask for help instead of charging ahead alone.

detail.description: You stand in a dim, wood-paneled room where the scent of aged paper and lamp oil lingers thick in the air. A single brass lamp hangs from the ceiling, casting long shadows over a sturdy oak desk cluttered with ledgers and ink-stained parchment. The floorboards creak underfoot, worn smooth by decades of hurried footsteps. A narrow stair leads upward, and a heavy door stands slightly ajar to the east, revealing a sliver of the next room. The faint sound of the tide lapping against the quay drifts in from the open outer door.
detail.lore: This is the main receiving room of the custom house, where incoming ship manifests and tariff ledgers are first sorted before being filed upstairs. Built a century ago when the port was young, its walls have absorbed the murmur of a thousand deals and the rustle of countless pages. The desk has belonged to the customs archivist for thirty years, and the lamp has never once been extinguished during working hours. The broken seal on the outer door was noticed at noon, but no one admits to having entered.

people.personality: Mara speaks in clipped, precise sentences, as if every word must be accounted for in a ledger. They are patient with those who share their respect for order but have little tolerance for carelessness or wasted time.
people.backstory: Mara Quill has been the customs archivist for the port since they were twenty-five, and they take pride in the fact that not a single manifest has gone missing under their watch—until now. The broken seal on the door has shaken their confidence, and they are determined to uncover who tampered with it and why. They believe the missing ledger holds the answer.
people.likes: order, quiet, well-kept records
people.conscious_desire: Mara wants to recover the missing customs record and restore the integrity of the ledgers.
people.unconscious_desire: Mara wants to prove that their system is flawless and that the breach was an anomaly, not a failure.
people.recognized_need: Mara must maintain the accuracy of the port's customs records, as their duty demands.
people.unrecognized_need: Mara needs to accept that no system is perfect and that mistakes, or even sabotage, can happen despite their best efforts.

readable.description: True only if this thing has WRITING on it that a player could read: a note, a letter, a label, a docket, a page, a sign, an inscription. False for everything else, which is most things.
